metadata.note: Skill teardown of skills/make/nbb/SKILL.md (episode.source_sha256 9b38c9ca…; SOURCE-SNAPSHOT SHA-256 395389a3…). The `nbb` skill takes any reel or lecture (or a whole book) and derives an NBB — @NikBearBrown-channel — cut of it: writes a NEW nbb- directory, scaffolds a beat_sheet.nbb.json with audience/palette/register/voice pre-set, and leaves a Claude-directed _variant_todo list for rewriting narration in the Teardown register, inserting an LLM exercise as the second-to-last beat, and appending the NikBearBrown outro. Standing rule: the canonical beat_sheet.json is NEVER modified. Two halves: brand_variant.py does the deterministic metadata scaffold (no spend); Claude does the creative rewrite guided by SKILL.md. Voice: Kokoro am_onyx — Liam in for Bear (IN-FOR-BEAR LAW). This teardown IS a claude-liam reel — outro is ClaudeTitleOutro (hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK); inner composer folder chip is @HumanitariansAI per playlist. brand_variant.py demoed live on demo/fixture-reel/ (three runs captured in demo/nbb-run.log: fresh scaffold, refuse-without-force, source-hash-unchanged proof).

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK-FIRST — the anatomy of the nbb skill: the doctrine, the scaffolder, the Teardown prose spec, the brand card, and the palette tokens.
beats.narration_text: First, the anatomy. On the toolkit side there is SKILL dot md — the doctrine, the standing rules, and the ending order. Next to it, scripts slash brand underscore variant dot py — a small deterministic scaffolder that copies your beat sheet into a new nbb dash directory. Then two style sources: prose slash teardown slash PROSE dot md, the Feynman times MKBHD register that Claude will rewrite against, and brands slash nbb dot md, the NikBearBrown brand card. And the teardown palette — white, ink, one red — exported from tokens slash vox dot ts. Small on disk. Sharp on purpose.

beats.role_note: The pipeline — five steps from `nbb [input]` to a review-ready NBB beat sheet.
beats.narration_text: The flow is five steps, and only the first is code. Scaffold — brand underscore variant dot py copies the beat sheet into a new nbb dash directory and presets audience, palette, register, engine, voice. That is the whole deterministic half. Then Claude does the rest. Rewrite every beat's narration in the Teardown register — take the machinery apart, judge the design choices. Insert one LLM exercise as the second-to-last beat — a paste-ready prompt and a dig-deeper follow-up. Append the NikBearBrown outro from AUTHOR dot md. Then verify the ending order: body, LLM exercise, outro. Same shape every reel.

beats.role_note: Design decision 1 — SOURCE IS NEVER MODIFIED. Every write lands in a new nbb- directory. Idempotent scaffold; refuse-without-force.
beats.narration_text: First design decision, and it is the whole safety story. Source is never modified. When brand underscore variant dot py runs, it writes into a brand new sibling directory called nbb dash your dash slug. Your canonical beat sheet dot json is not opened for write. It is opened for read, once. Run the command twice and the second run refuses — the nbb sheet already exists, and dash dash force is what you need to reset it from canonical. That is the isolation contract. Delete the nbb dash directory and you are back to a clean slate. Nothing you did to the derived cut can leak upstream.

props.heading: Source is never modified.
props.body: brand_variant.py writes into a NEW sibling directory: [book]/youtube/nbb-[slug]/. The canonical beat_sheet.json is opened read-only, once. beats.role_note: Design decision 2 — DETERMINISTIC HALF vs CREATIVE HALF. brand_variant.py does metadata (no spend); Claude does the register rewrite (guided by SKILL.md and PROSE.md).
beats.narration_text: Second decision, and it is the one that keeps the skill honest. Two halves. The deterministic half is the Python script — it presets audience, palette, register, engine, voice, typography, and outro source. It drops actual duration seconds on every beat so durations recompute for the new narration. No API calls. No spend. The creative half is Claude — rewriting every narration text in the Teardown register, adding the LLM exercise, appending the outro. That half is guided by SKILL dot md and by prose slash teardown slash PROSE dot md, not automated. The script never tries to be clever about voice. The register rewrite is a judgment call.

beats.role_note: Design decision 3 — THE LLM EXERCISE IS SECOND-TO-LAST. Paste-ready prompt + dig-deeper follow-up. Renders as a card, read by Liam.
beats.narration_text: Third decision. Every NBB cut ends the same way, and the second-to-last beat carries a specific shape. It is not a summary. It is a paste-ready LLM prompt. Two parts. Part one is a self-contained prompt with enough context that it produces a useful output on its own, without the video — you can drop it straight into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. Part two is a dig-deeper follow-up — a genuinely useful next question, not a recap. Liam reads both on screen. The card renders in the teardown palette. The prompt sends the viewer somewhere they can keep going.

beats.role_note: FALSIFIABILITY — Batch mode + the _variant_todo checklist. Boundary: nbb on a book folder scaffolds every reel + every lecture, but nothing runs the register rewrite for you. The _variant_todo IS a checklist, not code.
beats.narration_text: Falsifiability. Point nbb at a book folder and it batches — every reel under youtube slash and every lecture folder under lectures slash gets its own nbb dash sibling. All deterministic. All no-spend. But here is what it does not do. It does not automate the rewrite. Open the scaffolded beat sheet dot nbb dot json and you will find a field called underscore variant underscore todo — a five-item checklist for Claude to execute, in order. Rewrite in Teardown. Add the LLM exercise. Add the outro. Verify the order. Build. If you run brand underscore variant dot py on a hundred reels and stop, you have a hundred scaffolded shells and zero finished cuts. The register is a judgment call, not a loop.

Skip the checklist and you have shells, not cuts.

props.sparkLine: The batch is the easy half.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — artifact card. Recapitulates the skill in six lines.
beats.narration_text: The verdict. The nbb skill derives an NBB channel cut of any reel or lecture — new sibling directory, presets metadata, hands Claude a checklist. Source is never modified — the canonical beat sheet is byte-identical before and after. Two halves — deterministic scaffold in Python, creative rewrite in the Teardown register, guided by Claude. The second-to-last beat is always an LLM exercise — paste-ready prompt plus a dig-deeper follow-up. Voice is Kokoro am onyx, Liam in for Bear, IN dash FOR dash BEAR law. And the checklist is a checklist — brand underscore variant dot py never tries to be clever about voice.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer with a paste-ready dry-run prompt. Liam reads aloud + discusses. Safe: only scaffolds, never rewrites, never builds.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code. Read the nbb skill's SKILL dot md. Pick any delivered reel of your own — one you have already shipped, so nothing is at risk. Run brand underscore variant dot py against it with the nbb audience. That is the deterministic step — no spend, no rewrite, no render. Then check three things. Does a new sibling directory named nbb dash your slug now exist. Does its beat sheet dot nbb dot json carry audience NikBearBrown, palette teardown, engine kokoro, voice am onyx. And does your canonical beat sheet dot json have the same SHA dash two fifty six as before you ran anything. If all three answer yes, the isolation contract holds. Stop there — do not rewrite, do not render, do not compile.
